blocks: The SAM-1500C-12 inverter/charger owner's manual contains no occurrence of Modbus, RS-485, RS-232, baud, or any RJ-style jack — the only hits for 'remote' are marketing copy about remote housing and the standard FCC radio-interference boilerplate. It has no remote-control jack at all. The optional SAM RC on the plain SAM inverters is an on/off accessory with no published protocol.
refutedOnReview: REFUTED — and not merely unsupported: the grouping's own stated rationale is contradicted by Samlex's own documentation.  WHAT CHECKS OUT The cited PDF exists and is genuine. I downloaded it and extracted 117 KB of text (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lemarier-dev-solar/01a009b6-aeb2-4d8b-8a84-65ee02fe099b/scratchpad/sam1500c.txt`). The stated negative result is accurate for that one model: zero hits for modbus / rs
gotchas: SAM-1500C-12 is the odd one: it is an inverter/CHARGER (DeviceKind would be inverter, with a charger side), which normally implies charge-stage and a reason to want telemetry. It has none. Modified sine wave, no comms, no remote jack. Tier D — recorded so nobody hopes.
Modified sine wave across the SAM line. Relevant to load compatibility notes elsewhere in the catalogue, not to protocol.
The retailer's SAM-1500C-12 entry carried no protocol claim at all, which turns out to be the honest listing.
